observations: The strongest seasonal concentration is in Nov/Dec 2025, followed by a sharp post-holiday drop.
The manual payments series changes sign in 2026, turning negative in the later months.
Incentives are tiny compared with the other reimbursement lines and do not move the overall curve much.
The documents are structured as order-level reimbursement summaries, which matches the official Zé Seller API reports model.

official_api_confirms: Merchant KPIs are available by period with MONTH/WEEK/DAY/HOUR granularity.
Order reimbursement summaries are paginated and tied to a merchantId and a start/end date window.
Operational incentives are weekly summaries tied to isoYear and isoWeek.
The docs explicitly treat financial reporting as separate report families, not a single all-in-one profit ledger.
what_the_repo_data_can_say: Which weeks and months are strongest or weakest.
Which reimbursement components dominate the seasonal swings.
Which partner appears most frequently in the extracted reports.
Which products and drivers contribute most inside the current extracts.
what_it_cannot_prove_alone: True profit after every operational cost.
Total platform margin without company-side costs.
Causal reasons for the seasonal spike without external commercial context.

recommendation.plain_language: Use these JSONs as a clean business reading layer: the data clearly shows end-of-year seasonality and a manual-payment change, but the official API docs mean this is still a reimbursement/reporting view, not a full profit statement.
next_questions: Which products dominate the November/December peak?
Which weeks drive the manual-payment negative shift?
